title: Projectile

reference.basis: no object of known size is visible and no length is stated

slow_motion.evidence: no narration, captions, or on-screen text indicate slow motion

subjects.description: small glossy blue spherical ball in free flight

observation.what_happens: A blue ball moves rightward and downward across a light tiled wall. It is already airborne at the upper left at the start and is still airborne just above the brown floor at the lower right at the end.

calibration.note: scale from the fall itself: 4666 px/s² over 7 arcs = g of 9.807 m/s²

given: g = 9.807 m/s² (Earth); it set the scale, so treat g as known and fixed
reasoning: x grows steadily right while y shows ~5 sharp-bottomed parabolic arcs with peaks and troughs drifting down, classic bouncing flight not a pendulum or straight track. Candidates therefore keep ballistic x-y flight with a restitution bounce event, then add a downhill floor to explain falling trough levels and quadratic air drag for Earth air.

critique.finding: The ball flies in vacuum under gravity with g = {g} and hits a flat floor at {y_floor}. Each bounce keeps {e} of its vertical speed.
critique.headline: Bouncing ball flies freely and rebounds off floor
critique.why_it_won: The winner captures the single clean bounce on a flat floor while the sloped model adds tilt that never appears.

headline: Bouncing ball flies freely and rebounds off floor
finding: The ball flies in vacuum under gravity with g = 9.81 m/s² and hits a flat floor at -0.95 ± 7.36e-4 m. Each bounce keeps 0.88 ± 2.17e-4 of its vertical speed.

eyeball.law_in_words: Ball falls under constant gravity and on contact with the floor the normal velocity reverses and is scaled by the restitution, so rebound speed equals e times impact speed.
